subject: SLO-driven pricing pilot + archive cost split (Datadog / Grafana Cloud)
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLO-driven pricing pilot + archive cost split (Datadog / Grafana Cloud)

Team,

Quick note to start a short pilot proposal for Acme Retail. They asked whether we can run an SLO-aligned pricing pilot to compare Datadog and Grafana Cloud for two things: (1) active ingest/monitoring cost under an SLO-banded SLA, and (2) long-term archive retention and egress charge allocation for archived logs. They want a single recommendation and a way to split archive add-on charges across product teams.

Goals for the pilot (2 months):
- Measure cost per SLO band (P99 latency, error SLO) under representative traffic (we'll provide replay).
- Model 3-year archive costs for cold storage + retrieval and propose a chargeback methodology.
- Negotiate pilot credits + transitional pricing (Datadog & Grafana) to offset egress + hot-to-cold migration testing.

Ask: Marcus, can you draft an outline of the experiment config and the MAP (measurement + acceptance plan)? Ben, can you lead outreach to the vendor reps (Datadog / Grafana) and request pilot credits / a minimal PO for POC? Naomi, please flag any legal/contract constraints (data residency, log access for evaluation).

Attaching a quick MAP sheet with proposed metrics and guardrails (SLO-pricing-pilot-MAP.xlsx). I'll schedule a 30-min sync with Acme and vendor reps once we have draft asks.

Thanks,

Rachel Kim
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Attachment: SLO-pricing-pilot-MAP.xlsx (spreadsheet, 120KB)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLO-driven pricing pilot + archive cost split (Datadog / Grafana Cloud)

Thanks Rachel — saw the MAP. I added a short experiment plan and two configuration profiles in the sheet:
- Profile A: conservative (current retention 90d hot + 3yr cold)
- Profile B: aggressive (30d hot + 7yr cold)

Key technical notes:
- We'll need replay tokens for a 48-hour window to hit P99 tail behavior. Be explicit with vendors that KV cache and continuous batching need to be enabled for parity.
- Archive cost split proposal (draft): base infra split by ingestion volume, incremental retrieval charges allocated to business units that run ad-hoc investigations. Suggest a 70/30 split: 70% fixed (ingest/retention), 30% variable (retrieval egress).

I've flagged three items for procurement:
1) Pilot credits request (Datadog) - ask for $25k in pilot credits + 30-day extended trial on log rehydration.
2) Grafana Cloud - ask for a Grafana-managed Loki ingest trial and 50% discount on long-term storage during pilot.
3) NDA/access: ensure we get read-only access to vendor usage dashboards for the test window.

I'll draft vendor emails and attach the MAP with the experiment params.

- Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

Attachment: SLO-pricing-pilot-MAP.xlsx (updated)
From: Datadog Sales <sales@datadog.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Nelson <sara.nelson@acme-retail.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 11:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLO-driven pricing pilot + archive cost split (Datadog / Grafana Cloud)

Hi Ben / Rachel,

Appreciate the clear MAP — we can support a POC but need to clarify scoping and minimal billable PO/credits. Two quick notes:
1) Pilot credits: we can offer $20k in pilot credits covering ingest + indexing. Archive storage is handled through our S3-compatible cold tier; we can wave the first 30 days of storage but cannot absorb long-term egress unless we agree on a capped retrieval budget.
2) Access: we will provide a read-only org key and a telemetry dump export. Labs team will need the replay sample to calibrate indexing profiles.

Attached is a preliminary quote (dd-quote-2027-04.pdf) and a short pilot statement of work. We recommend the following acceptance criteria:
- P99 latency under target with continuous batching enabled
- Cost delta per million events vs Grafana Cloud below 15% for Profile A
- Successful week-long cold restore with retrieval under $X (to be mutually agreed)

If acceptable, I can set up a 30-min alignment call with our pilot engineering and pricing team for Friday.

Best,
Alex Ramos
Strategic Sales Engineer, Datadog
alex.ramos@datadog.com

Attachment: dd-quote-2027-04.pdf (vendor quote, 46KB)
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@datadog.com>, sales@grafanacloud.com
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Sara Nelson <sara.nelson@acme-retail.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLO-driven pricing pilot + archive cost split (Datadog / Grafana Cloud)

Thanks Alex — that is helpful. I'll propose the following next steps so everyone is aligned:

1) Alignment call: Friday, Apr 16 at 10:00am PT (30m) — Datadog pilot engineering + Grafana rep + Acme + Redwood. Aim: finalize replay window, agree on retrieval cap, and confirm dashboard access.
2) Vendor asks (for both vendors):
   - Pilot credits (aiming for $20k-$25k equivalence)
   - Read-only org usage dashboards for the test window and a one-off telemetry export
   - Agreement to a capped retrieval budget for cold restores (we'll model cost sharing if usage exceeds cap)
3) Procurement/legal: Naomi, please advise on minimal PO wording vs. trial MSA — we prefer a short SOW + PO for finance to run the pilot without full contract redlines.

Ben, please create a HubSpot record for this pilot (DEAL-1782) and log the vendor quote attachments. Marcus, update the MAP with final replay dates after the alignment call.

Looking forward — small pilot to inform a potential Dedicated/Private deployment billing recommendation.

Rachel
Rachel Kim
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com
